name: Isopropylhydroxylamine
description: Isopropylhydroxylamine (CAS 5080-22-8 ) is a hydroxylamine derivative used in industrial chemistry as a stabilizer and polymerization initiator. Its reactive N–OH functionality makes it effective for controlling oxidative degradation. This chemical is essential for managing radical-driven processes in polymer manufacturing. In plastics production, it functions as a controlled radical scavenger, helping regulate polymerization rates and molecular weight distribution. Rubber compounders use it as an antioxidant additive to extend the service life of vulcanized compounds exposed to heat and oxygen stress. It is particularly effective in specialty resins and high-performance materials. In printing and packaging, it supports formulation stability in ink systems where premature polymerization would compromise shelf life. It prevents oxidative degradation that can lead to viscosity changes or skinning in storage. Industrial cleaning and home care formulators incorporate it into systems requiring controlled reactivity. It helps in the stabilization of active ingredients during storage, ensuring consistent performance for the end user. Isopropylhydroxylamine is typically supplied as a liquid or aqueous solution, with concentration and purity specifications varying by application. Technical-grade material is the standard commercial offering for industrial use. Buyers should confirm purity levels, inhibitor content, and packaging specifications directly with the supplier.
